openings.claim: Downward hatch compression need not carry the sideways retention load. A removable rim-mounted guide pocket could locate the hatch through padded edge bearing while permitting vertical lift-out.
openings.delta: Remove increased left-corner compression as the hypothesized necessary action. Use the four supplied strips, drilled only in the strips, with bolts outside the hatch and rim to form two removable rim-only guide assemblies. Their hatch-edge bearing faces carry lateral load; they do not squeeze the hatch against its seal. Reopening lifts the hatch out, and cord keeps removed assemblies recoverable and clear of the marked opening. Exact assembly geometry remains unresolved.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, ordinary tighter left-corner pressing, guides should limit displacement to 1 mm under 20 N without requiring that pressing action or reproducing its opposite-corner lift. The final 1 mm card should not prevent positioning, reopening within 30 seconds, or leave a new visible seal tear. These are predictions, not supplied observations.
openings.probe: Within ninety minutes, first check whether strip-and-bolt geometry can capture the rim and provide edge bearing without modifying hatch or trough. If feasible, compare two configurations: ordinary left-corner pressing in two closure/pull trials, one disturbed; then the guide configuration through ten opening cycles and ten closure/pull trials, with the card on final closure. Use the scale, ruler, stopwatch and numbered cards; inspect seal after each cycle. Keep observations within twenty minutes.
assumptions: Rim accessibility, edge geometry, bolt reach and strip capacity are indispensable unknowns; the supplied dimensions do not establish guide feasibility.
Defeat occurs if the guides slip, require hatch compression or forbidden alteration, obstruct inspection, exceed available fabrication time, miss any outcome threshold, or tear the seal.

Success would refute necessity of extra downward compression for this fixture and pull; it would not establish that removing compression generally guarantees retention, or that compression necessarily fails.

assessment: One uncertain counterexample candidate; geometry and load-path feasibility must precede informative trials. This is a probe, not a deployment claim.
